mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.5 percentage points over the next 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the preceding 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 2% while UNRATE falls by 0.2 percentage points within the next 5 days
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS growth is not accompanied by UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided catalog, but as a proxy use HOUST for industrial production as a leading indicator) predicts stronger consumer demand, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positively correlated with the 6-month trend in HOUST (Pearson IC < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests supply-side strength that can outpace demand, causing S&P 500 forward returns to turn negative over the next 20 days as valuations adjust.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows by more than 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative when INDPRO growth exceeds 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates continued monetary accommodation, driving S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL stays below 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sub-2% CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a labor market tightening that increases wage growth expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive within 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when UNRATE crosses below 4.5% without a concurrent rise in wage growth proxies (not available).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in both retail employment (PAYEMS) and consumer confidence ( proxy via HOUST leading indicator) suggest expanding demand, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both increase in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST show no monthly increase.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent supply-side constraints (indicated by two consecutive months of decline in INDPRO), S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the next 20 days as market prices in slower growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative when INDPRO declines are not sustained over two months.
